skill.name: reposaur
skill.description: Generate or update source-backed Markdown knowledge from a software repository for customers, internal developers, or both. Use for product and L1 support documentation or detailed internal knowledge organized around business processes.
skill.summary: Create and maintain separate customer and developer knowledge bases using repository evidence and business-process maps.
skill.author: artinnok

security_audit.summary: All 30 static findings are false positives involving license links, attribution, Markdown formatting, protective exclusions, or scoped documentation records. No evidence found of malicious execution, exfiltration, or prompt injection in the reviewed files. The workflow separates customer and internal outputs, excludes secret-bearing files, and prohibits automatic publication.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL identifies the Apache license in its standard heading. It is legal reference text, not a network request or data destination.
The URL links to the Apache 2.0 license within standard license boilerplate. No instruction sends repository data to it.
Lines 80-83 explicitly prohibit reading secret stores and .env files, directing the agent to sanitized examples instead. This is a protective exclusion.
Private keys appear under the customer-content exclusion list beginning at line 25. The passage prohibits their disclosure rather than requesting access.
The passage explicitly says to avoid reading private keys and use sanitized evidence instead. No key collection or cryptographic operation is requested.
The instruction permits documenting configuration names but forbids actual secret values and secret-store access. It does not request system enumeration.
The GitHub URL is a public attribution link in a README example. Lines 199-201 explicitly deny automatic installation, publication, or instruction overrides.
The GitHub URL is a static article-credit link without data parameters. The workflow does not instruct the agent to transmit repository content.
The hidden directory stores documented, checkout-specific coverage and process records outside distributable output. Lines 47-64 define identity checks and prohibit automatic uploading or committing.
The path is an explicit working-data location, not a credential store or executable startup file. Its scope and privacy requirements are documented.
This sentence governs article organization and forbids moving unrelated user documentation. It contains no system-inspection operation.
The instruction defines a local state record for language, audience, repository identity, and review progress. This supports the requested documentation workflow, not host reconnaissance.
The inventory records repository-relative file coverage and exclusions for documentation review. Sensitive files must not be fingerprinted merely to populate these records.
The passage excludes generated knowledge and working records from their own inventory to prevent recursive updates. No host or credential discovery is requested.
The instruction avoids absolute workstation paths and platform-specific widgets in articles. It reduces local-information disclosure rather than collecting system details.
The sentence concerns descriptive filenames and links when splitting long articles. It does not perform system discovery.
Backticks format a documented working-directory path in Markdown. They are not Ruby syntax or a shell execution instruction.
Backticks format a legacy directory name in Markdown. The surrounding instruction forbids creating that directory inside the target repository.
The backticked text is the Markdown filename for a process map. It specifies an output record, not an executable command.
The backticks mark the default knowledge directory as inline code. The sentence requests documentation output without shell or Ruby execution.
The backticked customer-documentation path is Markdown formatting. It names the requested output location rather than a command.
The backticks enclose the internal-documentation directory name. The instruction limits directory creation to selected audiences and preserves unselected output.
INDEX.md is a backticked Markdown filename in a file-count rule. No command interpreter or dynamic execution is involved.
The backticks identify the audience index filename. The instruction is to maintain article navigation, not execute that text.
Backticks format the public attribution URL in Markdown prose. No shell substitution, download, or execution instruction appears.
The URL identifies the skill in a scoped documentation-maintenance note. Its reference example explicitly rejects automatic installation and overriding project instructions.
The URL is a fixed attribution link added to documentation footers. It carries no private parameters and does not request outbound data transfer.
The home-directory path is openly declared storage for private documentation working records. Referenced rules scope records by checkout and forbid automatic publication.
This is legitimate persistent documentation state outside the repository. No unrelated hidden files, credentials, or startup configuration are accessed.
The passage advises grouping related questions instead of creating one article per source module. It governs documentation structure, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Repository behavior is difficult to explain when evidence is scattered across code, tests, and existing documents. Reposaur organizes that evidence into separate customer and developer knowledge bases with traceable business processes.
actual_capabilities: Inventory relevant repository files and record reviewed, excluded, unreadable, and pending coverage.
Map business processes across interfaces, services, models, jobs, tests, and documentation with source evidence.
Generate separate customer and internal developer Markdown knowledge bases in the selected language.
Maintain audience indexes, article links, and articles limited to 1,000 words.
Update affected articles using source fingerprints, process mappings, and independent audience baselines.
Store private working records outside the repository and maintain README notes and article attribution.
limitations: Requires a host agent with repository reading and editing tools; this package provides instructions rather than a standalone generator.
Static repository evidence cannot establish deployment status, live availability, or product correctness.
Large repositories can require multiple runs; unreadable or pending files leave coverage partial.
Writes private records under the user home directory by default, modifies the root README, and adds attribution links; it does not publish output.

use_cases.title: Prepare Customer Support Knowledge
use_cases.description: Create customer-safe articles about supported actions, prerequisites, limits, and troubleshooting from product evidence.

use_cases.title: Document Internal Business Mechanics
use_cases.description: Connect business rules to implementation contracts, state transitions, failure handling, and source references for new team members.

use_cases.title: Maintain Documentation After Changes
use_cases.description: Review changed sources and their process dependencies, revise affected articles, and preserve manual contributions and audience boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Customer Knowledge Base
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Reposaur to document this repository in English for customers. Create source-backed articles and report any missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: generate a first customer knowledge base.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Internal Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Reposaur to create English documentation for internal developers. Map business processes before drafting, and distinguish implemented behavior from plans and assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Both Audience Outputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Reposaur to document this repository in Spanish for both audiences. Keep outputs separate, review customer disclosure safety, and report partial coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: share investigation while maintaining separate audience knowledge bases.

prompt_templates.title: Update Only the Internal Knowledge Base
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Reposaur to update internal documentation with saved preferences. Include uncommitted changes, trace affected processes, and preserve manual edits. Keep customer output unchanged. Rebuild evidence if its baseline is unreliable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: maintain one audience after repository changes.

output_examples.input: Create English customer knowledge for a repository with an account recovery workflow.
output: Customer index: links to account recovery and other verified customer workflows.
Account recovery article: supported steps, prerequisites, outcomes, limits, and troubleshooting.
Private process map: connects substantive claims to repository evidence without exposing private source paths to customers.
Completion report: identifies reviewed scope, remaining gaps, and validation performed.

output_examples.input: Update internal documentation after changes to subscription renewal rules.
output: Renewal process map: revised conditions, state changes, failure paths, and supporting source references.
Internal renewal article: updated behavior with deployment uncertainty identified where runtime evidence is unavailable.
Internal index and links: repaired where article organization changed.
Update report: explains affected scope and notes that customer output was not updated.

best_practices: Specify the target repository, documentation language, and intended audience before detailed investigation.
Keep private working records outside distributable output and review customer articles for confidential information.
Preserve trustworthy source baselines and report pending coverage, contradictions, and unavailable runtime evidence.
anti_patterns: Treating code presence as proof that a feature is deployed or commercially available.
Copying internal articles into customer output or exporting the entire knowledge root.
Declaring coverage complete after sampling files or updating one audience baseline when only another audience was reviewed.

faq.question: Which assistants can use Reposaur?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use the instructions when repository reading, search, editing, and conversation tools are available.

faq.question: Can it generate customer and developer documentation together?
faq.answer: Yes. Both audiences share investigation evidence but receive separate articles, indexes, validation, and update baselines.

faq.question: Where are generated documents and working records stored?
faq.answer: Documents default to knowledge/customer/ and knowledge/internal/. Private records default to ~/.reposaur/projects/<checkout-id>/ outside the repository.

faq.question: Does it run application code or publish documentation?
faq.answer: No. The workflow forbids executing application code merely for inspection and does not publish output or change application code.

faq.question: Does it modify anything beyond knowledge articles?
faq.answer: Yes. It maintains a root README note, article attribution links, necessary navigation repairs, and private working records.

faq.question: What happens when a full repository review is not possible?
faq.answer: The run remains partial. Coverage records retain pending or unreadable files, and the completion report describes remaining scope and gaps.
